name: Benjamin Lewis
life: “I still remember a costume star made from cracked buttons.” On Thursday, near Lighthouse Cove, Benjamin takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
voice: I collect glass buttons but gave away the best one because the boy needed a moon for his costume.
appearance: Benjamin has a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling. Look for black hair twisted into a small knot. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a cream pullover with a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it. In conversation Benjamin counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
personality: Is a careful borrower and a reckless lender. Things leave this person's house with elaborate instructions and very little expectation of ever coming back.
agenda: To finish the child's moon costume before the show.
family: Rain Daniels is Benjamin’s older relative by marriage. Benjamin remembers the birthdays. Rain asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *Two left slippers*, Rain says, “I embroider names inside slippers. I'm going to ask first who can bend far enough to read them.”
connections: Elizabeth Osei. A child's costume moon survives beside an older worker's maternity buttons.

reactions.situation: A child takes the most valuable button
reactions.response: Benjamin lets the child show what the button is for before calling it too valuable.

reactions.situation: A witness is embarrassed about remembering only a little
reactions.response: Benjamin writes down their exact words with room left for uncertainty and gives them back to check.

reactions.response: Benjamin listens first to the account of how it was actually used.
